title: Window Tool Panel with Recursive Category Groups
description:
All windows must have a tool panel on the bottom left. Tool node groups (e.g. selection) act as categories. When a group tool node is activated, the panel expands with another line. This works recursively. There can only be one active group per level (at most one active per level; zero active collapses that line).

Implementation per approved plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-all-windows-must-cheerful-llama.md:
1. Render the bottom-left toolbar overlay + WindowToolbarChrome unconditionally on every Window (ui/js/react/index.tsx), with a disabled unfold toggle when there are no tools.
2. Add groupToolNodesByCategory in framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx to synthesize category collections (selection/tools/actions/history/sync) from a window's top-level tool nodes, matching wgpu's partition_tools_by_category ordering; wire into windowToolbarNode.
3. Rewrite buildToolbarRibbonSegments/reconcileToolPath so collections never auto-activate: at most one active group per level, zero active collapses the line, no leaf-only-sibling flattening, no single-collection auto-drill. Update ToolTree's picker onValueChange so re-clicking the active toggle collapses that line and deeper lines.
4. Add "tools"/"sync" to UiToolbarParentCategory i18n plus De/En entries; extend resolveControlLabelId to resolve window-scoped ui.toolbar.<windowId>.group.<slug> ids.
5. Sweep plugin tools()/mode_tools Rust implementations (writer, cad, s, sequence, procedural, draw, note, trinity, layout, shooting, process, lowpoly) to tag top-level tool nodes with explicit .with_category(...).
6. Extend existing tests (framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts toolbar-ribbon describe, ui/js/react index.tsx i18n test) and existing stories (.storybook/stories/ui/Toolbar.stories.tsx, Window.stories.tsx) — no new files.
summary:
Fixed 6 of 8 scanned violations of the single-script.ts-per-directory convention: (1) repo/client/vscode had no script.ts — added one wrapping dev/test/build/lint/build-vsix, project.json now calls `bun ./script.ts <target>`; (2) mathematical/graph/dsl/core had no script.ts and ran raw `bun test` — added script.ts with a test command, project.json updated (still 0 test files in that package, same pre-existing gap, just now routed correctly); (3) repo/lib/js/package.json's "test" script bypassed nx/script.ts with a duplicated raw `bun test` command — now calls `bun ./script.ts test`, matching what project.json already did; (4) compose/client/ui/desktop's .compose-test.mjs imported a one-off test/defineConfig.mjs — inlined defineDesktopTestConfig and deleted the extra file (test/suite/index.mjs stays separate since Electron's main process loads it by file path at runtime, not via import); (5) deleted orphaned root test-export.ts (unwired Playwright smoke script, no references anywhere); (6) deleted orphaned framework/renderer/react/wasm-session-loader.test-stub.ts (dead mock, no references anywhere).

Deliberately left as exceptions with documented rationale, not violations: .devcontainer/*.sh (7 scripts) and repo/native/bootstrap/{script.sh,script.ps1} are pre-Bun bootstrap artifacts — post-create.sh installs Bun itself so it cannot depend on script.ts running first, compose-entrypoint.sh is Docker's ENTRYPOINT contract, neo4j-mcp-run.sh is invoked by fixed external MCP client configs; root script.ts's own NativeOsScript already documents this same exception. Also left eslint.config.mjs, repo/lib/js/nx-plugin.mjs, .vscode-test.mjs, pw-loader.mjs untouched — their filenames are dictated by ESLint/nx/@vscode/test-cli/Playwright tool contracts.

Verified: `bun ./script.ts` (vscode) prints correct usage/routes; `bun ./script.ts test` (graph-dsl-core) fails identically to the old raw `bun test` (0 test files — pre-existing gap, not a regression); the inlined .compose-test.mjs still resolves its default export correctly via dynamic import. Note: repo/lib/js's actual `bun test ./index.test.ts` run fails with a pre-existing, unrelated issue (root script.ts prints its usage line on import) — confirmed via `git diff` that script.ts/index.test.ts/index.ts are untouched by this ticket, so this is a pre-existing bug outside this ticket's scope, not something introduced here.
